title: Instrumental 7: 3rd-Declension Feminine and Adverbial Use
titleRussian: Творительный 7: Третье склонение и наречная форма
description: Feminine nouns ending in soft -ь (дверь, ночь, площадь) take -ью in the instrumental. The bare instrumental of time-of-day and season nouns also serves as adverbs: ночью (at night), утром (in the morning), летом (in summer).
descriptionRussian: Существительные женского рода на мягкий -ь принимают окончание -ью. Творительный падеж слов, обозначающих время суток и время года, употребляется как наречие: ночью, утром, летом.
intro: Two unrelated things share this lesson. The soft-sign feminines take an ending that appears nowhere else in the case, so they are worth learning as a set. And the words for morning, evening, winter and summer are frozen instrumentals doing adverb duty: when you say 'in the morning' in Russian you are using this case without noticing.
rules: Feminine nouns ending in soft -ь (3rd declension) take -ью in the instrumental: дверь → дверью, ночь → ночью, площадь → площадью, кровать → кроватью.
Two nouns add a stem extension: мать → матерью, дочь → дочерью. The longer stem (мат-ер-, доч-ер-) appears in every case except nominative and accusative singular.
The bare instrumental of time-of-day and season nouns serves as an adverb: утром (in the morning), днём (in the afternoon), вечером (in the evening), ночью (at night), весной, летом, осенью, зимой.
These adverbial forms use the regular instrumental endings: -ом / -ем for masc / neuter (утром, вечером), -ой for feminine -а (весной, зимой), -ью for feminine -ь (ночью, осенью).
examples: Лена стоит за дверью. (Lena stands behind the door.) дверь → дверью.
Маша работает ночью. (Masha works at night.) Adverbial: ночью.
Я люблю гулять летом. (I love walking in summer.) Adverbial: летом.
Антон ходит на работу утром. (Anton goes to work in the morning.) Adverbial: утром.
Маша гордится дочерью. (Masha is proud of her daughter.) дочь → дочерью (stem extension).
Зимой здесь холодно. (In winter it's cold here.) Adverbial: зимой.

rows.label: день
cells: in the daytime, in the afternoon

items.promptEnglish: The cat is sleeping under the chair.
items.hint: Recall L6: stative position with под takes which case?
items.explanation: Warm-up from Lesson 6. Спит is stative; под + instrumental for static location → стулом. Today's lesson adds two more pieces: 3rd-declension feminine -ь and the adverbial bare instrumental.

items.hint: Дверь is a 3rd-declension feminine noun. What ending does it take in the instrumental?
items.explanation: Дверь ends in soft -ь, putting it in the 3rd declension. The instrumental ending for these nouns is -ью: дверью. The form does not match the regular feminine -ой / -ей; it's its own pattern.

items.hint: 'At night' uses the bare instrumental of ночь, which serves as an adverb.
items.explanation: Ночь is feminine -ь (3rd declension), so the instrumental is -ью → ночью. The bare-instrumental form also serves as an adverb meaning 'at night.' This is one of the most common adverbial uses of the instrumental.

items.promptEnglish: I (m) walk in the park in the morning.
items.hint: 'In the morning' uses the bare instrumental of утро, used adverbially.
items.explanation: Утро is neuter -о, so the instrumental is -ом → утром. As an adverb, утром means 'in the morning.' The same pattern gives вечером (in the evening) from вечер.

items.promptEnglish: Anton is proud of his mother.
items.hint: Гордиться + instrumental. Мать has a stem extension before its endings.
items.explanation: Мать is a 3rd-declension feminine noun with a stem extension: every case except nom-acc singular uses the stem мат-ер-. The instrumental adds -ью to the extended stem: матерью. Дочь works the same way: дочерью.

items.promptEnglish: It is very cold here in winter.
items.hint: 'In winter' is the bare instrumental of зима, used adverbially.
items.explanation: Зима is feminine -а, so the instrumental is -ой → зимой. As an adverb, зимой means 'in winter.' The seasons all behave this way: весной (spring), летом (summer), осенью (autumn, 3rd-decl), зимой (winter).

blanks: Маша часто читает _____. (Masha often reads in the evening.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Вечер is masculine consonant. The bare instrumental serves as the adverb 'in the evening': вечером. The same -ом ending you saw in Lesson 1 for masculine instrumental nouns; here the form just acts as an adverb.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The cat is sleeping behind the bed.
errorCorrection.explanation: Кровать is a 3rd-declension feminine noun (ending in soft -ь), so its instrumental ending is -ью, not the regular feminine -ой: кроватью. Кроватой applies the -ой ending of regular -а nouns to a 3rd-declension noun and is not a valid form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Grandmother has always been proud of her daughter.
errorCorrection.explanation: Дочь takes a stem extension -ер- before its endings in every case except the nominative/accusative singular, so the instrumental is дочерью (stem доч-ер- + -ью), not дочью. Дочью skips the extension and is not a real form.

errorCorrection.sentence: Антон любит гулять осень, когда прохладно.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton likes to walk in autumn, when it is cool.
errorCorrection.explanation: 'In autumn' is expressed by the bare instrumental of осень used as an adverb: осенью. Осень is 3rd-declension feminine, so the instrumental ending is -ью. The bare осень (nominative/accusative) does not express time on its own.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Masha is proud of her daughter.
minimalPairs.explanation: Гордиться takes the instrumental. Дочь is 3rd-declension with a stem extension: дочерью. The nominative дочь cannot follow a verb that requires a case form.
'At night' is the adverbial bare instrumental of ночь: ночью (3rd-declension -ью). The accusative ночь would mean 'I often read [the] night,' which doesn't fit any standard reading.

reviewVocab.definition: third declension (feminine nouns ending in soft -ь; in the instrumental they take -ью: дверь → дверью)
at night (adverbial use of the instrumental of ночь; also the regular instrumental form of the noun)
mother (instrumental form, with the stem extension мат-ер-: мать → матерью)
